# PoC: process-affine message capabilities across Temporal boundaries (issue #77)

Smoke-test evidence for `PROCESS_AFFINE_CAPABILITY`: serializable tokens in `msg`
(`msg._linkSource`, `msg._session`) whose *meaning* depends on process-local state
retained elsewhere in the Node-RED runtime (a live socket, a live callback map).

This is a **PoC/evidence branch only** — nothing here is merged into `main`. See
issue #77's final verdict comment for the required classification table.

## Environment

- `main` tested: `67c1060d937b2c868695baa30c0bc01ddf8d07ae`
- Single combined worker (`createCombinedWorker` via `make run`), real Temporal
  dev server (`temporal server start-dev`), real external clients (Node's `ws`
  and `net` modules) — no mocked node methods.
- Editor/admin ports overridden (`EDITOR_PORT=18880 ADMIN_PORT=18881`) only
  because the default `1880` was occupied by an unrelated host process; no
  functional difference from the documented defaults.

## Fixtures

| File | Case |
|---|---|
| `flow-p1-link-call-return.json` | P1 — Inject → Link Call → Link In → Change → Link Return → Debug |
| `flow-p2-websocket-reply.json` | P2 — WebSocket In → Change → WebSocket Out (reply to same session) |
| `flow-p3-tcp-reply.json` | P3 — TCP In → Change → TCP Out (reply mode, same connection) |
| `ws-client.js` | real `ws` client used to drive P2 |
| `tcp-client.js` | real `net` client used to drive P3 |

Deploy any of these with a full v2 deploy against a running runner B, e.g.:

```bash
FLOW=$(node -e "console.log(JSON.stringify({flows: require('./flow-p1-link-call-return.json')}))")
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18881/flows \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Node-RED-API-Version: v2' -H 'Node-RED-Deployment-Type: full' \
  -d "$FLOW"
```

## P1 — Link Call / Link Return

Triggered `POST /inject/inj1`. Temporal Workflow `ingress-1790006879947-mioit1ghx9`
ran 4 sequential `executeNode` Activities (`lc1` → `chg1` → `lr1` → `dbg1`),
`WorkflowExecutionCompleted` with `lastNode: "dbg1"` — i.e. the call returned to
the **original continuation after the Link Call node**, not just to the Link In
target.

Captured `msg` at each hop (decoded from the real Temporal history):

```
lc1  DONE -> chg1: msg._linkSource = [{ id: "bc6ec5e17a1fba1eb2f8be13b7d0", node: "lc1" }]
chg1 DONE -> lr1:  payload = "hello-processed", _linkSource unchanged
lr1  DONE -> dbg1: _linkSource consumed, msg._event = "node:lr1"
dbg1 DONE -> []
```

`_linkSource` itself is plain, serializable JSON (an array of `{id, node}`) and
survived the Activity boundary with zero special handling — this part is
portable. What is **not** portable is the correlation itself: Node-RED's stock
`link call` node (upstream, untouched — `@node-red/nodes/core/common/60-link.js`)
keeps a process-local `Map` of in-flight calls keyed by that `id`, holding the
live `send`/`done`/timeout callbacks for the *calling* node instance. Resolving
`link return` only works because the `link call` Activity (`lc1`) and the
`link return` Activity (`lr1`) executed as `executeNode` Activities in the
**same combined-worker process**, sharing that Map. If `lc1` and `lr1` were
Activities dispatched to two different Activity-worker processes (issue #70's
split-runner topology) on the same Task Queue, whichever runner didn't own the
original `lc1` invocation would have no entry for that call id and the return
would silently fail (or worse, resolve against nothing) once the queue is
serviced round-robin by multiple pollers.

**Classification: `PASS_SINGLE_RUNNER_PROCESS_AFFINE`.**

## P2 — WebSocket reply to originating session

Real `ws` client connected to `ws://127.0.0.1:18881/ws/echo`, sent `"ping"`.
Temporal Workflow `ingress-1790006938921-03u57meu5ef7` shows the captured `msg`:

```
chgws DONE -> wsout: msg._session = { type: "websocket", id: "59888a436b71499a" }, payload = "ping-reply"
```

Client received `"ping-reply"` on the **same** connection. `_session` is plain
JSON and serialized cleanly through Temporal's default payload converter.

- **Serializes:** yes, plain JSON.
- **Single runner:** PASS — reply reached the originating client.
- **Restart behavior:** held a connection open, then `make stop` mid-session —
  client observed `close(1006)` immediately (abnormal closure). The
  `websocket-listener` config node's live socket registry is in-process
  memory only; there is no reconnect/resume of the old session, by design.
  A brand-new connection after `make run` again works fine (new session id),
  confirmed live.
- **What runner-local state the token refers to:** the `websocket-listener`
  config node's live `ws` socket map, keyed by session id, held in the process
  that accepted the TCP connection.

**Classification: `PASS_SINGLE_RUNNER_PROCESS_AFFINE`.**

## P3 — TCP reply to originating connection

Real `net` client connected to `127.0.0.1:9977`, sent `"ping"`. Temporal
Workflow `ingress-1790007024413-d01edflwkpn` shows:

```
chgtcp DONE -> tcpout: msg._session = { type: "tcp", id: "be0651e4e362e2e5" }, payload = "ping-tcpreply"
```

Client received `"ping-tcpreply"` on the same TCP connection.

- **Serializes:** yes, plain JSON, identical shape to the WebSocket case.
- **Single runner:** PASS.
- **Restart behavior:** identical to P2 — a held-open connection was dropped
  (`close` with no data) the instant the runner process was stopped. No
  reconnect/replay of the in-flight session.
- **What runner-local state the token refers to:** the `tcp in` node's live
  `net.Socket` reference, held in the accepting process's connection pool.

**Classification: `PASS_SINGLE_RUNNER_PROCESS_AFFINE`.**

## P4 — Dashboard client affinity

**Classification: `NOT_RUN`.**

Reason: issue #64 (FlowFuse Dashboard 2.0 PoC) closed without leaving behind a
committed, reusable flow fixture for its client-affine (`msg._client.socketId`)
path — its evidence was gathered via a one-off Playwright session against a
manually-built flow, not a checked-in fixture. Reconstructing a minimal
client-affine Dashboard flow (a widget path that is genuinely per-socket rather
than broadcast/state-setting) is not "trivial reuse of #64" as the issue
requires, and building new Dashboard infrastructure here would expand scope
beyond a smoke test. `_client.socketId` shares the same architecture as
`_session` above (a plain JSON token naming a live Socket.IO connection held in
resident `ui-base` state), so the same `PASS_SINGLE_RUNNER_PROCESS_AFFINE`
outcome is the expected result if this is picked up later — this row is left
`NOT_RUN` rather than asserted without direct evidence.

## Optional multi-runner probe

Not run. All three tested cases already show the identical process-affinity
root cause (a runner-local registry — the `link call` pending-call `Map`, the
`websocket-listener` socket map, the `tcp in` connection pool — keyed by a
plain, portable token) without needing a second poller to demonstrate it: the
architecture already implies a two-runner topology would route the follow-up
Activity to whichever runner happened to poll it next, with no guarantee it's
the one holding the live resource. Building a real two-runner harness to prove
this empirically is exactly the "runner affinity / connection routing" design
question that belongs to issue #70, not this smoke test — see the Conclusion
below and #77's final verdict comment.

## Small fixes

None. No generic bug was found — `msg` in all three cases is already plain
JSON and Temporal's default payload converter serialized it with zero special
handling in every case. `httpNodeBridge.js`'s live-object-snapshot pattern is
the correct answer for genuinely non-serializable state (`req`/`res`); nothing
here needed that treatment because `_linkSource`/`_session` were never
non-serializable to begin with — the problem is purely about which *process*
holds the live resource the token names, not the token's JSON-ness.

## Architectural findings

No new issue opened. This PoC's findings feed directly into the two issues
already scoped for this:

- **#69** (contrib-node compatibility classification) — recommends that
  `PROCESS_AFFINE_CAPABILITY` be defined precisely as: *token is portable JSON;
  the runner-local resource it names is not.* `link call`/`link return`,
  `websocket in`/`out`, and `tcp in`/`out` (reply mode) should all be
  classified this way, not `PASS`/`FAIL` alone.
- **#70** (split Workflow/Activity-runner topology) — this is where the actual
  fix (if any) belongs: either pin the follow-up `executeNode` Activity for a
  `link return`/session-affine reply to the same Activity-worker process that
  owns the live resource (a Task-Queue-per-runner or session-affinity
  scheduling scheme), or explicitly document these node types as
  single-combined-runner-only.

## Conclusion (proposed generic rule for #69)

A capability should be classified `PROCESS_AFFINE_CAPABILITY` (not
`PASS`/`FAIL` alone) when **all** of the following hold:

1. the `msg` token itself is plain, serializable JSON (no live object,
   function, or class instance);
2. resolving/using that token later requires a runner-local, in-process
   registry (a `Map`, a socket table, a connection pool) that is not itself
   part of the Workflow/Activity input or output;
3. a single combined-worker process (today's default) hides this dependency
   because the registry is trivially shared by every Activity invocation;
4. splitting Activity execution across multiple runner processes (issue #70)
   would non-deterministically place the follow-up invocation on a runner that
   may not hold the required live resource, with no error surfaced by
   Temporal itself — only by the node's own logic (a callback never firing,
   a reply silently going nowhere).

`link call`/`link return`, `websocket in`/`out`, and `tcp in`/`out` (reply
mode) all satisfy this definition today. Any future contrib-node smoke test
that finds a live-socket, live-timer, or live-callback token behind a
serializable id should apply the same four-point test rather than inventing a
new category per node type.
